chapter: Las Vegas, Sinatra and later years
title: Backing Sinatra with six men
summary: A Goodman gig at Basin Street East, then a Sinatra benefit led Sinatra to use Norvo's six-piece group at the Fontainebleau and the 500 Club; Bill Miller had been in his earlier band.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: Sure, and that's the band that Benny Goodman would hire when he would go to Europe, we had Bill Harris and Flip Phillips, and maybe Gene DiNovi, and we worked here at Basin Street, East. We came back here, I don't know
if you remember when we worked there .
Well maybe I wasn't here then.

Then I'd go back and go back to the Sands or that same five pieces with Bill Miller, we did a benefit with Sinatra in Los Angeles . Just six men. And he liked it. So he said, that's what I'm going to -- that's what we'll use that's a great idea. So we went to the Fontainebleau, yeah, first we went to the Fontainebleau and in Florida with that group. That's all he used behind him, just six of us, you know, it was like -- it was really a shocking revelation. See him come out. Cause, he had -- one of his ideas was to for me to come out and play a number, like a regular band, and go up to the mike and say, 'Now, I'd like for you to meet our boy singer,' and he'd come out walking out, swinging his arms like a young boy singer --
You were just talking about when you were backing Sinatra. And you said --
Well then we made trips with him, we played the 500 Club -- And we just used the six men.
And course you realize that Bill Miller was in that band with Mildred and I. That he's -- (unintelligible) with Sinatra.
Sure, and the band that I had at the Blackhawk.
Yes, that's before I went with Barnett.
Before I broke up. So the six pieces was --
Course you -- you could give Sinatra color. For his backgrounds that he liked to have.
Both the light swing and -- and Lightweight,
And if we could afford to have a thing (unintelligible) going on that made it good harmonic structure, which we did. It went down pretty good.
So then when we'd go to Australia he'd take us and maybe add over there.
Sometimes in Sydney we had a big band.
